bob_acme: Hey team — since yesterday (~16:30 UTC) we've been seeing a high volume of streaming requests fail with a 'broken pipe' on our side. The client sees a 502 from your gateway and we get curl exit code 56. Looks like client disconnects mid-stream but your metrics spike 5xx. Repro steps below, can you advise?

jess_support: Sorry about that — can you paste a minimal repro and the correlation id? Also which model and region?

bob_acme: Repro (simplified):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk.xxxxx" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","prompt":"hello","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -v
```
Run that and then ctrl-c after first chunk. Correlation id from our logs: c-id=abc123-1789. Gateway log: `2026-03-02T16:18:43Z request=c-id=abc123-1789 stream-write:error write failed: broken pipe proxy=gateway-7 status=502`

kai_engineer: ack, tagging @sam_runtime @maria_sre. This looks like client-side TCP close (EPIPE / ECONNRESET) while gateway is writing. Gateway currently converts write errors during streaming into 502, which inflates our 5xx. We should map these to a client-abort category (499) and not count as server-side failures.

sam_runtime: digging in runtime: we do surface syscall errors as internal writer errors and then bubble up a 502. On chunked paths the upstream sometimes already sent partial 200 + chunks; the write failure is the netstack telling us client closed. I'll add specific detection for EPIPE/ECONNRESET on write and set a synthetic 499-like code and new metric `stream.client_abort`.

maria_sre: also saw a latency bump correlating with the spike window. Could be client keepalive + proxy timeout interplay. Are their clients intentionally closing early after a few tokens?

bob_acme: yes — their client infra often cancels the request after seeing an initial chunk (they read partial then cancel). We can reproduce by sleeping 1s then closing.

jess_support: thanks — could you paste the full gateway trace for one of those c-ids?

bob_acme: snippet: `2026-03-02T16:18:43Z request=c-id=abc123-1789 stream-write:error write failed: broken pipe
proxy=gateway-7 status=502
client_ip=1.2.3.4` and client curl: `* Connection #0 to host api.redwood.ai left intact
*   Trying 1.2.3.4...
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (1.2.3.4) port 443 (#0)
* SSL connection using TLS1.3_ECDHE...
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
`

kai_engineer: OK. Sam, please open RFC/PR to change classification and add metric/label. Also update analytics pipeline so BigQuery/metrics don't count `stream.client_abort` as 5xx in SLO calculations.

sam_runtime: will do. Plan: 1) add detection for EPIPE/ECONNRESET -> tag request as client_abort; 2) emit `stream.client_abort` (counter + last_seen); 3) ensure response status in logs is set to 499_stub so downstream analytics can map it; 4) add unit + integration tests with chunked encoding and client close. I'll target a canary rollout.

deploy-bot: deploy job queued: runtime/gateway r1892 (canary) -> gw-canary-3. CI status: tests=passing, lint=ok.

maria_sre: Also recommending we tune proxy keepalive to be more forgiving for short-lived clients, and add a dashboard for `stream.client_abort` and a decomposition in the 5xx panel to exclude that label. I'll create a small runbook entry for oncall.

kai_engineer: assigned ENG-RUNTIME-402 for follow-up and tracking. Add post-deploy verification steps: run the repro curl and ensure gateway logs `client_abort` and analytics show `stream.client_abort` increment without 5xx bump.

jess_support: To customer: short-term workaround — modify client to not close TCP immediately after first chunk, or add a short jittered delay before aborting. Also add exponential backoff and retry on 5xx while we fix classification. We'll keep you posted on progress.

sam_runtime: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1245 — implements mapping and metric. Requesting review from @kai_engineer. Unit tests included for chunked stream with early client close.

deploy-bot: canary deploy succeeded on gw-canary-3 at 2026-03-02T22:14:50Z. No 5xx spike seen when running customer's repro against canary; `stream.client_abort` increments as expected.

maria_sre: canary looks clean for 2h. Scheduling prod rollout at 2026-03-03 00:30 UTC if no regressions. Alert thresholds updated: removed `stream.client_abort` from 5xx SLO calc and added new panel.

bob_acme: great, we'll run a wider set of repros tonight and report any failures. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

jess_support: ETA for prod rollout: 2026-03-03 00:45 UTC. We'll update thread post-rollout and attach rollback steps + runbook. :thumbsup:

sam_runtime: post-deploy action items: 1) merge PR, 2) prod deploy + smoke tests, 3) backend analytics mapping change (GH: infra/metrics PR 987), 4) add note in docs about streaming error classification.

maria_sre: leaving a short oncall note: if 5xx > baseline after prod deploy, immediately rollback and check for false-positive client_abort mapping.

jess_support: thanks everyone — keeping this thread open until prod rollout completes and customer confirms repros.
